overall: AG found the Board's Complaint Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law at its May 28 meeting, because G.L. c. 112, § 65C exempts investigative conferences before an order to show cause. The 2013 meeting dispute was not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleges the Complaint Committee unlawfully barred his stenographer and supporters from its May 28 meeting on a complaint against him.
allegations.key_passage: However, there is a specific law that excludes certain activities of the Board from the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleges the Committee failed to post notice of its May 28 meeting as the Open Meeting Law requires.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee's investigatory conference was exempt from the Open Meeting Law's requirements, it did not violate the law by failing to post

allegations.summary: Complainant alleges the Committee held an open meeting in January 2013 under similar circumstances and that the May 28 meeting was improperly handled differently.
allegations.key_passage: We take no position on  this dispute, and  consider only the question of whether  the May 28 meeting complied with the Open Meeting Law.
